Build quota-aware sending/reading (per-user budget of 6,000 units/min; messages.send costs 100 units)
Draft per-scope justifications and the Limited Use compliance statement
Audit your scope list against Google's official tier tables before you submit

approval.cost: Free from Google; the CASA assessment is paid to a Google-approved assessor, and Google publishes no price (third-party figures of roughly $500-$4,500 are unofficial)
approval.trigger: Always: brand verification (prerequisite) plus scope verification. Sensitive scopes (gmail.send): stated at typically 3-5 business days. Restricted scopes (anything that reads mail): potentially several weeks, PLUS an annual CASA security assessment if the app accesses restricted data from or through a server, re-certified every 12 months from the assessor's Letter of Assessment date.
approval.wait: Days for send-only; several weeks plus assessment time for read access

blockers.detail: gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.metadata, and the full-access scope are all restricted. Even gmail.metadata (headers and labels, no message body) is restricted. The moment an agent reads mail server-side, the full apparatus applies: restricted verification, demo video, annual CASA assessment.
blockers.howToClear: Design send-only if you can: gmail.send is sensitive-tier and skips CASA entirely. If you must read, budget weeks and an annual assessment into the product plan.
blockers.title: Reading mail in any form puts you in the restricted tier

blockers.detail: You may only request Gmail scopes if your app is one of: a built-in/web email client, an automatic email backup app, a productivity-enhancement app (Google's own examples include CRM, mail merge, and generative AI summaries), or a reporting/monitoring app that benefits the user. Prohibited: mobile keyboards, one-time/manual email export apps, spam distribution, multi-account policy abuse.
blockers.howToClear: Frame the product honestly into a permitted category before submitting; if your app fits none, restricted Gmail scopes are not available to you at any price.
blockers.title: Your app must fit a permitted application type

blockers.detail: IMAP, POP, and SMTP access requires the single full-access scope https://mail.google.com/ (read, compose, send, permanently delete everything). There is no granular IMAP scope, and to be approved an IMAP app must show full utilization of that scope.
blockers.howToClear: Use the Gmail API's granular scopes instead of IMAP/SMTP unless you are genuinely building a mail client.
blockers.title: IMAP/SMTP forces the maximum scope

tested: Read-only verification: Gmail scope tier tables, permitted application types, Limited Use texts, CASA mechanics, push-notification rules, and quota figures were checked against current developers.google.com and support.google.com pages (no project created, nothing submitted)
unverified: CASA assessment cost and duration: Google states neither; third-party figures (~$500-$4,500, 2-6 weeks) are unofficial.
Detailed AL1 vs AL2 assessment mechanics live on the App Defense Alliance site, not a Google domain.
No fixed Gmail data-retention period is stated in the Limited Use texts; the enforceable duties are deletion on user request, deletion documentation, and privacy-policy disclosure.
The 3-5 business day sensitive-scope figure comes from Google's sensitive-scope verification doc, not a Gmail-specific page.

flavor.recommended: A Google Cloud OAuth client (Web application) requesting Gmail API scopes; there is no separate 'Gmail OAuth app'
flavor.why: Gmail rides on Google's OAuth platform: same project, consent screen, and verification machinery as the Google guide. What is Gmail-specific is the scope tier table and the Gmail API policies, and those decide your timeline. Choose gmail.send alone for send-only agents (sensitive tier, no security assessment); anything that reads mail is restricted tier.

humanMust: Decide the tier: send-only vs read access (this is a product decision, not an implementation detail)
Frame the app into a permitted application type and write the per-scope justifications
Record the demo video (English, consent screen, each scope shown in use)
Publish a privacy policy disclosing Gmail data use, including the Limited Use compliance statement
Contract a Google-approved assessor and complete CASA if you use restricted scopes server-side
name: Gmail
nuances: Limited Use rules bite AI products specifically: you may not pool users' Gmail data to train or improve a general ML/AI model (per-user personalization is allowed), may not use the data for ads or sell it, and your support staff may not read users' emails to debug except under narrow exceptions. You must publish an explicit Limited Use compliance statement.
gmail.modify is restricted, despite at least one community source calling it sensitive; Google's official scope table is authoritative.

Push notifications are a build project: Gmail push runs over Cloud Pub/Sub, you must renew users.watch at least every 7 days (daily recommended), notifications carry only {emailAddress, historyId}, and delivery is capped at 1 event/sec per watched user with occasional drops, so a periodic history.list fallback is officially recommended.

Per-user quotas are tight for agents: 6,000 quota units/min per user per project, and messages.send costs 100 units, so roughly 60 sends or 100-300 message reads per minute per user. Max 500 recipients per message.
gmail.settings.sharing is effectively closed to normal apps: administrative use only, Workspace customers, service account with domain-wide delegation.

Worked example (send-only notifications): an agent that emails users alerts about something they follow needs only gmail.send. That is sensitive tier: brand verification plus scope verification in days, no CASA, no annual assessment. The same product redesigned to also read replies would jump to restricted tier and the full assessment apparatus.
prerequisites: A Google Cloud project with the Gmail API enabled (platform setup per the Google guide: branding, verified domain, External audience)
A product that fits one of Google's permitted Gmail application types
A privacy policy that discloses Gmail data access/use/storage/sharing and states Limited Use compliance
Your minimal Gmail scope list, chosen tier-first (see steps)

steps.detail: Create the Google Cloud project, branding, External audience, and OAuth client exactly as in the Google guide, then enable the Gmail API in the API library. There is no Gmail-specific console.
steps.title: Set up the Google OAuth client

steps.detail: This is the decision the whole guide hangs on. Send-only (gmail.send) = sensitive tier, verification in days, NO security assessment. Anything that reads mail, even headers only (gmail.metadata), = restricted tier, weeks of review plus annual CASA if server-side. Typical full agent (read + send + organize) = gmail.modify, one restricted scope that cannot permanently delete. Never request scopes for unimplemented features; Google explicitly prohibits it.
steps.title: Choose your Gmail tier first

steps.detail: Confirm your app fits a permitted type (email client, automatic backup, productivity enhancement incl. generative AI summaries, or user-benefit reporting/monitoring). Write a per-scope justification explaining why this scope is necessary for this live feature; reviewers push downscoping hard (their example: an app that only occasionally sends email must not request full access).

links.label: Workspace user data and developer policy

steps.title: Fit a permitted application type, write justifications

steps.detail: Publish branding first, then submit in the Verification Center with an unlisted YouTube demo video: full OAuth grant flow in English, consent screen with the correct app name, client ID visible in the address bar, and each scope's functionality shown in use. Scopes in code must match the console's Data Access page exactly or users get the unverified-app screen.
steps.title: Submit verification with demo video

steps.detail: Only for restricted scopes used from/through a server: after all other verification steps, Google's Trust and Safety team initiates the CASA assessment with an approved independent assessor (AL1 or AL2 by risk). Passing yields a Letter of Assessment; re-certification is due at least every 12 months from its date, and adding a new restricted scope may trigger reassessment. The assessment also verifies you can delete user data on request.
steps.time: Final step of review; annual thereafter
steps.title: (Restricted, server-side only) Complete CASA

steps.detail: Implement with Gmail's mechanics in mind: tokens encrypted at rest, data encrypted in transit; if you need realtime mail events, build the Pub/Sub push pipeline (topic, publish grant to gmail-api-push@system.gserviceaccount.com, users.watch renewed at least every 7 days) and budget per-user quota (6,000 units/min; send = 100 units).
steps.time: ~Half a day to a day of coding
steps.title: Implement Gmail-specific mechanics

tagline: There is no separate Gmail OAuth app; you register a Google client and request Gmail scopes. Your scope choice is the whole game: send-only takes days, reading mail takes weeks plus an annual security assessment.

time.active: Platform setup ~1 hr + ~2-4 hrs of justifications, privacy policy, and demo video
time.total: About a week for send-only; several weeks to months for read access (restricted verification + CASA)
time.waiting: Sensitive scopes typically 3-5 business days (stated); restricted scopes potentially several weeks (stated), plus assessment scheduling
